# Marky v1.5.0

Images work now. Opening a vault imported from Obsidian used to show a broken
icon everywhere a picture should be, and there was no way to get a new one into
a note at all. This release covers all three routes: rendering what is already
there, pasting, and dragging in from Finder or Explorer.

### Images in notes

- **Local images render.** The asset protocol was never enabled, so a webview
  served from `tauri://localhost` could not read a single file off disk. It is
  on now, and every image target is resolved to a real path before rendering.
- **Paths resolve the way other editors write them.** Tried in order: relative
  to the note, relative to the vault root, then by bare filename against an
  index of the vault's media. Percent-encoded spaces, `../` walks and absolute
  paths all work; remote and `data:` URLs are passed through untouched.
- **Obsidian embeds.** `![[image.png]]` — a bare name with no path, which is how
  most Obsidian vaults store images — renders in both Read and Live modes, with
  `|300` and `|300x200` sizing honoured. The markdown grammar had no notion of
  this syntax, so Live mode needed a parser extension of its own.
- **A missing file says so.** An image whose file is not where the note claims
  now draws a dashed frame with its alt text, instead of collapsing to nothing
  and reading as if the app lost the picture.

### Adding an image

- **Paste.** Cmd/Ctrl+V puts a screenshot straight into the note, saved into the
  workspace and linked relative to it. A placeholder holds the spot during the
  write and is taken back out if it fails. Pasted images are named the way
  Obsidian names them, so a vault moving between the two apps keeps one scheme.
- **Drag and drop.** Drag an image in from Finder, Explorer or Files. A caret
  tracks the pointer through the text and the image lands exactly where it is
  pointing, on its own line. Files are copied without their bytes ever crossing
  into the frontend, so a large photo drops as quickly as a small one.
- **Attachment folder.** Where new images are saved is configurable under
  Settings → Editor. Defaults to `attachments/` under the workspace root; leave
  it empty to keep them beside your notes.

### Fixed

- **Screenshot filenames broke their own links.** macOS names every screenshot
  with a narrow no-break space (U+202F) before the meridiem. It is not an ASCII
  space, so it survived URL encoding — but the markdown parser counts it as
  whitespace, ended the link there, and left the raw markup sitting in the note
  as text. All whitespace is encoded now, not just the ASCII kind.
- **The first paste always failed** with "you don't have permission to save this
  image". Not the operating system: `fs:allow-exists` carried no path scope of
  its own, and in Tauri a scope attached to one `fs:allow-*` covers only that
  command. Checking whether a filename was taken was therefore refused for every
  path. All filesystem commands now share one scope, so this cannot recur one
  command at a time. A scope violation also no longer disguises itself as an OS
  permission error.
- **The drop caret sat away from the pointer**, drifting further the lower you
  dragged. Tauri types a drag position as physical pixels, but only Windows
  sends one — macOS reports AppKit points and Linux reports GTK widget
  coordinates, both already in CSS pixels, and the runtime relabels them without
  converting. Scaling by the device pixel ratio therefore halved an already
  correct coordinate on every Retina display. The sidebar's folder targeting was
  off by the same amount and shares the corrected conversion.
- **Dragging over the tab bar was treated as dragging into the text.** In
  auto-height mode the editor grows to fit the whole note and an outer container
  scrolls, so the editor's box extends far off the top of the window. Hit testing
  is now clipped to the part of the editor actually on screen.

### Notes

Exported HTML keeps the paths you wrote rather than the app's internal asset
URLs, which resolve to nothing outside Marky.

Links already written by an earlier version are not rewritten. A note whose
image link broke on the U+202F bug needs that line deleted and the image added
again.
